s1.syndrome_frame: Pruritic, violaceous, annular skin lesions in a localized area
salient_findings: Discrete, dark red, circular lesions in the right axilla
Severe pruritus at the lesion sites
Lesions are well-circumscribed, violaceous, and annular without scale or erosion
key_facts: Male patient in his 40s
3-month history of skin lesions
Lesions are limited to the right axilla
Severe pruritus wakes the patient up at night
No recent trauma or history of similar lesions
No associated pain, blisters, or systemic symptoms
No improvement with over-the-counter hydrocortisone cream, ketoconazole cream, or discontinuation of underarm deodorant
Biopsy findings show lymphocytes obscuring the dermal-epidermal junction
Wood lamp examination was negative

shortlist.label: Granuloma annulare
shortlist.why_kept: Annular skin lesions with lymphocytes obscuring the dermal-epidermal junction on biopsy

shortlist.label: Erythema annulare centrifugum
shortlist.why_kept: Pruritic, violaceous, annular skin lesions in a localized area

shortlist.label: Lichen planus
shortlist.why_kept: Violaceous, annular patches with severe pruritus

shortlist.label: Annular lichenoid dermatitis of youth
shortlist.why_kept: Annular skin lesions with severe pruritus, limited to one area

shortlist.label: Mycosis fungoides
shortlist.why_kept: Pruritic, violaceous skin lesions with lymphocytic infiltration on biopsy

raw.rationale: The presence of violaceous, annular patches with severe pruritus and biopsy findings showing lymphocytes obscuring the dermal-epidermal junction are characteristic of lichen planus.

rejected.label: Granuloma annulare
rejected.why: Typically presents with papular lesions, not violaceous patches

rejected.label: Erythema annulare centrifugum
rejected.why: Usually has a more rapid progression and clearing of lesions

rejected.label: Mycosis fungoides
rejected.why: Typically has a more prolonged course and may involve the mucous membranes
